testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: rebase-check job (pull_request-only branch-currency assertion, not meaningful in a worktree of origin/main); proc-macos job (node --test tests/proc.test.mjs on macOS) (subsumed by the full suite on this macOS host); smoke-omp job (needs pinned omp installed via bun, absent here); install-and-smoke job (needs pinned omp installed via bun and network, absent here).

survived.claim: The documented `replace #N` procedure (tick-rows.md:111 sends it to phase-0.md's NEED resume steps, which say `ledger.mjs row <N> "impl-<N>-b"`) is now refused with exit 2 mid-run, because row N holds the settled `impl-<N>=PR#<M>` of the closed PR, and the PR did not update either doc although tick-rows.md:113 says the old PR's token should stay on that 'two-PR row'.
survived.evidence: probe.sh case 2 against copy/plugin/scripts/ledger.mjs, ledger row `#7 impl-7=PR#20 → PR#20`: `row 7 impl-7-b` → `ledger: row #7: drops settled member token 'impl-7=PR#20' — …` exit=2, row unchanged; `row 7 "impl-7=PR#20 → PR#20 · impl-7-b"` → exit=0. Doc text from `sed -n 650,664p references/phase-0.md`: "Record it the ordinary way — `ledger.mjs row <N>\n\"impl-<N>-b\"`"; `sed -n 104,120p references/tick-rows.md`: "`replace #N` — the `NEED resume` procedure (phase 0): `impl-<N>-b` … Its new PR settles onto the same row, and that two-PR row is a legitimate shape". The ticket's triage asked which flows legitimately drop a member token with `row`; this one is not addressed in the diff (only references/ledger.md changed).
survived.suggested_fix: In phase-0.md's NEED resume step (and SKILL.md:74's pointer to it), spell the row write as `ledger.mjs row <N> "<text> · impl-<N>-b"` — the row's current text plus the replacement, as tick-rows.md's `release #N` line already does — so `replace #N` mid-run carries `impl-<N>=PR#<M>`; a cross-run resume with no carried row stays `"impl-<N>-b"`.

votes.reason: Ran snapshot ledger.mjs in a scratch repo with row `#7 impl-7=PR#20 → PR#20`. `row 7 "impl-7-b"` gave exit=2 `drops settled member token 'impl-7=PR#20'`, and the row stayed unchanged. phase-0.md:658 still documents exactly `ledger.mjs row <N> "impl-<N>-b"`, and tick-rows.md:111-113 still says the new PR settles onto the same two-PR row. The diff doesn't touch either doc, so the documented replace procedure is refused as claimed. This is a direct probe, not a test-suite red/kill. Not checked: whether the replace flow is meant to use a different command in practice. I did not run the probe or build a copy; this verdict rests on reading the snapshot. phase-0.md:658 sends the replacement through `ledger.mjs row <N> "impl-<N>-b"`. tick-rows.md:113 says the new PR settles onto the same row and calls that two-PR row legitimate. ledger-grammar.mjs `settledMemberRefusal` refuses any `row` rewrite that omits a settled member token, which is any member token with an outcome, such as `impl-7=PR#20`. The refusal returns the message the claim quotes, `drops settled member token …`. The ledger.md text I read (line 121) says the same and names no exception for a replacement. I did not check whether the row still holds the settled token when `replace #N` is sent, so that step is inferred from the claim's own scenario. I did not confirm that the PR left phase-0.md and tick-rows.md unchanged, so that part is from the claim, not checked. unverified.claim: Because duplicates are counted, a row that already holds the same settled token twice (a violation of rowWriteRefusal's own 'unique members: one token per member, live or settled' rule) can no longer be cleaned with `row`; the only fix left is hand-editing ledger.md, which the skills discourage.
unverified.evidence: probe.sh case 4: row `#9 impl-9=bailed · impl-9=bailed`, `row 9 impl-9=bailed` → `drops settled member token 'impl-9=bailed'` exit=2. One way this shape arises: `settle` rewrites every bare copy on a row (ledger.mjs:2695 `.map((w) => (w === name ? token : w))`), so `impl-9 · impl-9` becomes two settled copies. I did not reproduce the settle path end to end.
unverified.suggested_fix: Count settled tokens by distinct text (a Set) rather than as a multiset, so dropping a duplicate copy is allowed and dropping the last copy is still refused. Or keep the multiset and say in the refusal text how to repair such a row.

unverified.claim: The check compares settled tokens byte for byte while parseToken accepts `applied:<head>` case-insensitively, so a rewrite that changes only the case of a fix-applier's head is refused as a dropped token (harmless but stricter than the grammar).
unverified.evidence: probe.sh case 5: row `#30 fix-pr-30=applied:abcdef1`, `row 30 fix-pr-30=applied:ABCDEF1` → `drops settled member token 'fix-pr-30=applied:abcdef1'` exit=2.
unverified.suggested_fix: No change needed if byte-exact preservation is intended, which matches the doc's 'as the row holds it'. Otherwise normalise the head's case before comparing.

unverified.claim: The new settled-token refusal makes pull.mjs's two ledger row writers exit 2 on a row that holds a settled member token. They write a replacement row (`impl-<N> · tier=…` in stage_row, `excluded · <token>` in answer_collision) and never carry the row's settled tokens. The Pull then stops with `ledger.mjs row failed` and the ledger is untouched. It is a loud stop, not a swallowed error.
unverified.evidence: In the copy I ran the argv pull.mjs builds. `ledger.mjs --file L row 3551 'impl-3551-b · tier=slow-high'` on `#3551 impl-3551=bailed · tier=smol-high` exited 2 with `row #3551: drops settled member token 'impl-3551=bailed' — a rewrite must carry every settled member token…`. `row 3551 'excluded · behind-issue:#3'` exited 2 the same way, and so did `row 7 'excluded · behind-issue:#3'` on `#7 impl-7=PR#9 → PR#9 · ports=1`. The ledger file was byte-identical afterwards. The shortlist path skips rows that hold an impl token (pull.mjs:1228), so only `next --head <N>` for a ticket whose row already has a settled impl can reach this. tests/ledger.test.mjs:3941 was edited to carry `impl-3551=bailed` in its re-Pull row call, and no pull.test.mjs fixture covers a settled row.
unverified.suggested_fix: Decide whether `pull.mjs next --head <N>` should handle a settled row. If it should, have stage_row and answer_collision read the row and carry its settled tokens. If it shouldn't, say so in pull.md. Either way, add a pull.test.mjs case for it.

unverified.claim: settledMemberRefusal protects only a token that parses with no error and has an outcome. A settled token whose outcome is malformed, and a `=`-less live token, can still be dropped by `row` with only the stderr `dropped:` line. The doc comment and the new test state this on purpose, so I found no unintended swallow.
unverified.evidence: Ran the grammar unit test and the new `row lets a rewrite add, drop or change a live member token…` test; both pass. I read the parseToken source. A token with an outcome outside its family's vocabulary returns `error !== null` and is excluded by the filter. A rewrite that adds one is refused by the existing malformed-token die at ledger.mjs:781.

unverified.claim: No finding above suggestion: every mutation I applied to the new settledMemberRefusal was killed. A few are killed only by a thrown TypeError (removing the `t !== null` guard) rather than an assertion about that guard.

unverified.claim: The added ledger.md text defines the refused token as 'any member token carrying an outcome'. The same paragraph then says a malformed member token may still be dropped. A malformed token also carries an outcome, so the two sentences conflict. The code refuses only tokens with no parse error and an outcome.
unverified.evidence: settledMemberRefusal filters on `t !== null && t.error === null && t.outcome !== null` (ledger-grammar.mjs:19-22). The ledger.md:121 added text says 'any member token carrying an outcome ... A live member token, and a malformed one, may still be dropped'. The test 'row lets a rewrite add, drop or change a live member token, and drop a malformed one but never add one' pins that a malformed token can be dropped.
unverified.suggested_fix: Reword the parenthetical to 'any well-formed member token carrying an outcome'.

unverified.claim: PR body: it says 'the drop-and-warn test now drops a live member token instead of a settled one'. In the diff, that test ('row names every token a rewrite dropped on stderr...') keeps its drop assertions on non-member and arrow tokens, and its fixtures now carry the settled `impl-5=PR#9`. The live-token drop is a new `live` fixture added to the same test (a row holding `impl-6`), not a swap of a settled drop for a live one.
unverified.evidence: Diff hunk at tests/ledger.test.mjs @@ -4105: the old `dropped`/`several`/`none` rewrites now include `impl-5=PR#9`, and `const live = tokenFixture(t, ["#6 impl-6 · ports=16326"])` is added as a new case.
unverified.suggested_fix: Say the test now carries the settled token in each rewrite and gains a live-token drop case.

unverified.claim: settledMemberRefusal can never refuse a new row (oldLine === null), yet it still parses every word of `line` before reaching that result; an explicit early return, as cellChangeRefusal already does, makes the no-op case clear and removes the null branch from the `settled` helper.
unverified.evidence: Ran node simplify/probe.mjs in the measuring copy. The rewrite `if (oldLine === null) return null; const settled = (text) => text.split(/\s+/).filter(isSettledToken);` was compared with the shipped settledMemberRefusal over 14×13 (oldLine, line) pairs, covering null, the test's mixed row, duplicates, changed outcomes, malformed tokens and extra whitespace, using assert.equal. Output: `pairs equal: 182`.

unverified.claim: The new `t !== null && t.error === null && t.outcome !== null` predicate copies the one settledOnLedger already uses for `## Dispatched` (line 659). The same settled test appears a third time at line 664. A shared `isSettledToken(word)` helper would keep the definition of 'settled' in one place, so the readers and this write guard cannot drift apart.
unverified.evidence: grep `error === null && .*outcome !== null` over plugin/scripts/*.mjs returns ledger-grammar.mjs:527, :659 and :664. In probe.mjs, `const isSettledToken = (w) => { const t = parseToken(w); return t !== null && t.error === null && t.outcome !== null; }` was used inside the simpler settledMemberRefusal (182/182 pairs equal). Over [impl-1=PR#2, fix-pr-3=bogus, merge-bot-1, finisher-pr-4=labelled], the helper gave the same names as settledOnLedger([], …): `[ 'impl-1', 'finisher-pr-4' ] [ 'impl-1', 'finisher-pr-4' ]`.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add `export const isSettledToken = (word) => { const t = parseToken(word); return t !== null && t.error === null && t.outcome !== null; };` near parseToken. Use it in settledMemberRefusal (`text.split(/\s+/).filter(isSettledToken)`) and in settledOnLedger's dispatched loop (`if (isSettledToken(e)) settled.add(parseToken(e).name)`, or keep the parsed t). Line 664 has an extra PR-bound clause and could share only the base predicate.

unverified.claim: The test helper `named` escapes `#`, `=` and `:` with `.replace(/[#=:]/g, "\\$&")`, but none of these is a regex metacharacter, so the escaping does nothing. The module-level `SETTLED_DROP` constant is used only in this one place, through `.source`. Writing the pattern directly would read more plainly.
unverified.evidence: Ran in probe.mjs: for each token in [impl-5=PR#9, fix-pr-12=applied:abcdef1, finisher-pr-12=labelled, impl-6=PR#12], the escaped and unescaped `new RegExp(`'${tok}'`)` gave the same .test() result on exact, suffixed, prefixed and wrong-PR inputs (assert.equal, printed `regex escape no-op: ok`). `grep SETTLED_DROP|const named` in tests/ledger.test.mjs shows SETTLED_DROP defined at 4125 and used only at 4129.
unverified.suggested_fix: const named = (token) => new RegExp(`drops settled member token '${token}' — a rewrite must carry every settled member token as the row holds it`); and drop the SETTLED_DROP constant. Keep the escape only if a later token may contain regex metacharacters such as `.` or `+`.
